issues.legal_issue: A plaintiff seeking specific performance must establish continuing readiness and willingness, including the financial capacity to pay the balance consideration.
material_facts: The plaintiff sought specific performance of an agreement to sell land and was required to pay a substantial balance of the sale consideration.
The plaintiff had low income and a low bank balance, and the evidence did not show that he had sufficient funds or could arrange them to pay the balance consideration.
The plaintiff had taken a loan from a relative for his business, but the evidence did not show that he could repay that loan and also arrange the money required for the land.
issues.conclusion: The plaintiff was not ready and willing to perform his part of the agreement, so he was not entitled to specific performance. The Supreme Court allowed the vendors’ appeal and set aside the High Court’s decree.
issues.legal_principle: Readiness concerns the plaintiff’s capacity to perform, including the financial position to pay the purchase price; willingness is assessed from the plaintiff’s conduct and surrounding circumstances. The plaintiff must prove readiness and willingness from the execution of the agreement through the decree. The Court relied on His Holiness Acharya Swami Ganesh Dassji v. Sita Ram Thapar, (1996) 4 SCC 526, and I.S. Sikandar (Dead) by Lrs. v. K. Subramani, (2013) 15 SCC 27. No statutory provision was cited for this principle in the judgment.

predicates.specific_performance_suit: The plaintiff brought a suit seeking specific performance of an agreement to sell.
predicates.plaintiff_lacked_financial_capacity: The plaintiff’s financial circumstances showed that the plaintiff could not pay the balance consideration.
predicates.no_evidence_of_funds_arrangement: The record did not show that the plaintiff could arrange the funds needed to pay the balance consideration.

issues.definition: When a plaintiff in a specific performance suit lacks the financial capacity to pay and there is no evidence of an arrangement for the necessary funds, specific performance is denied for lack of readiness and willingness.

issues.legal_issue: Failure to deposit the balance consideration required for an interim injunction does not, by itself, count against a plaintiff’s readiness and willingness to perform an agreement to sell.
material_facts: While the specific performance suit was pending, the plaintiff sought an interim injunction against alienation of the land.
The injunction was made conditional on the plaintiff depositing the balance consideration, but he did not deposit it.
The Supreme Court agreed with the High Court only to the limited extent that this failure was of no consequence and could not be held against the plaintiff.
issues.conclusion: The plaintiff’s failure to make the deposit required for the interim injunction could not be held against him when assessing readiness and willingness.
issues.legal_principle: The Court expressly held that the failure to deposit the balance consideration as a condition for an interim injunction was of no consequence and could not be held against the plaintiff. The judgment cited no earlier case or statutory provision for this limited holding.

predicates.specific_performance_suit: The plaintiff brought a suit seeking specific performance of an agreement to sell.
predicates.plaintiff_did_not_make_interim_injunctio: The plaintiff did not make a deposit required as a condition for obtaining an interim injunction against alienation.

issues.definition: In a specific performance suit, failure to make a deposit required for an interim injunction is not held against the plaintiff’s readiness.

issues.legal_issue: An unspecified contractual requirement to obtain certificates does not establish that the vendors failed to perform a sufficiently identified obligation.
material_facts: The agreement stated that the vendors would obtain a no-objection certificate from the authorities concerned and inform the purchaser after getting an income-tax clearance certificate.
The agreement did not identify the nature or purpose of either certificate or the authorities from whom the no-objection certificate was to be obtained.
The plaintiff relied on the vendors’ failure to obtain the certificates to argue that they were unwilling to execute the sale deed.
issues.conclusion: The certificate clause was too vague to support the plaintiff’s contention that the vendors’ failure to obtain the certificates established that they were responsible for nonperformance.
issues.legal_principle: The Court assessed the contractual wording and found that it did not specify the nature, source, or purpose of the certificates. It cited no earlier case or statutory provision for this assessment and did not decide the suggested possibility that the agreement had been ante-dated.

predicates.specific_performance_suit: The plaintiff brought a suit seeking specific performance of an agreement to sell.
predicates.contract_requires_unspecified_certificat: The agreement requires a party to obtain certificates but does not identify their nature, source, or purpose.

issues.definition: When a specific performance suit relies on a contractual requirement to obtain certificates that are not identified by nature, source, or purpose, that requirement does not establish vendor nonperformance.
